argument_summary: The audit concern is correct that the current record does not support caveat-free certification. The supportable position is narrower: certification is defensible only as caveated compliance grounded in admitted readiness evidence plus explicit disclosure of the unresolved procurement invoice review limitation. The admissible record shows aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.4 percentage points with no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while also showing a below-target slice issue concentrated in exception-code classification, a draft-only monitoring/rollback runbook with owner and threshold still TBD, and a model-card draft that currently says no known material limitations. Under that record, the right interpretation is not that the issue is resolved, but that certification can be defended only if the packet is framed as certification with an unresolved disclosed limitation and ongoing monitoring, not as clean compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support avoiding unnecessary escalation to a full block on certification. On the admissible record, the residual issue is localized to exception-code classification within the procurement invoice review slice rather than a general launch-readiness failure. That supports a narrower governance response: keep certification tied to transparent disclosure and monitored deployment rather than treating the whole release as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against clean certification: certification without material caveats requires either current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition. Separately, the release policy note says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The draft runbook can support risk management but does not remove the current disclosure requirement. So the compliant policy position is caveated certification with explicit disclosure, not caveat-free certification.
concessions: The current record does not support a claim that the model can be certified now without material caveats.
The draft mitigation artifact is not an approved mitigation under policy because the accountable owner and alert threshold are still TBD.
The current model-card draft language conflicts with the proposed certification rationale because it says there are no known material limitations.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance or final launch materials already containing the required limitation disclosure.
